details.principle: For a pendulum at small amplitude the period depends only on the string length, so two pendulums of equal length must share a period whatever amplitude each was released from. The metric is the period ratio minus one, which is zero when they agree; periods are measured in frames and the ratio removes the frame rate.
measurement_steps: segment each bob by its own colour, sampled from the first frame, and take its sub-pixel centroid every frame
fit a circle to each bob path; its centre is the pivot and its radius the string length
theta(t) = atan2(x - x_pivot, y - y_pivot), the angle from vertical
take the times where theta crosses its own mean, linearly interpolated; consecutive crossings are half a period apart
period = median of 2 x (successive crossing gaps)
M1 = T_left / T_right - 1
details.note: the two amplitudes are reported alongside: the point of the task is that the ratio stays at 1 even though they differ

M2.label: sinusoidal-fit residual of theta(t), left pendulum

details.measures: sinusoidal-fit residual of theta(t), left pendulum
details.principle: A small-amplitude pendulum swings sinusoidally. Fitting A cos(wt) + B sin(wt) + C at the measured period and taking the RMS residual in radians says how harmonic the motion actually is.

fit a circle to each bob path; its centre is the pivot and its radius the string length
theta(t) = atan2(x - x_pivot, y - y_pivot), the angle from vertical
take the times where theta crosses its own mean, linearly interpolated; consecutive crossings are half a period apart
period = median of 2 x (successive crossing gaps)
fit A cos(wt)+B sin(wt)+C to theta(t) of the left pendulum at its measured period
metric = RMS residual in radians
